title: Jurisdiction, Licensing and How to Verify Current Rules

content.overview: Cultivation legality is jurisdiction dependent. Learners should know how to identify the controlling authority and locate current primary regulatory information rather than treating a course, search result or old rule summary as legal authorization.

vocabulary.definition: The geographic or legal authority under which a rule or license applies.
Formal permission required by an applicable law or regulatory program.
An official law, regulation, agency rule, license document or authoritative government publication.

sections.title: Start with the location
sections.body: The controlling cultivation rules depend on where the activity occurs and what crop/activity is involved. USDA's hemp framework, for example, may operate through a state, tribal or USDA program depending on location.

sections.title: Use official sources
sections.body: Current agency sites, statutes, regulations and license materials are stronger than forum posts or old summaries. Rules can change, so verify the version and effective date before acting.

sections.title: Educational content is not a license
sections.body: Completing a THC Academy course demonstrates educational achievement only. It does not grant permission to cultivate, possess, process, transport or sell cannabis or hemp.

workedExamples: A grower moving operations to another state should re-check the controlling program rather than assuming the previous license or rules transfer.
If an old guide conflicts with a current agency page, verify the current regulation and effective date before relying on the guide.
commonMistakes: Assuming one state's rules apply nationally.
Treating hemp and non-hemp cannabis rules as interchangeable.
Treating a training certificate as legal authorization.
content.practicalApplication: For any proposed regulated activity, record the location, crop/activity, controlling agency, current rule or license source, effective date and unresolved questions before taking action.
content.summary: Regulatory literacy means knowing how to verify the rule that actually applies. Location, activity, authority and current primary sources come before operational decisions.
